L3·N10670unmasked layer
Mostly a weak/noisy detector: it fires on word-internal continuation sub-tokens that complete a longer word or proper name (the "-or" of Equinor, "-ine" of Refine, the "f" joining "Caliope|fertilizer", the "](" of a markdown link) plus a few impersonal informational words ("examples", "know"), while it is strongly suppressed by direct conversational second-person address tokens ("you", greeting "!", "of course").

Fires on boundary/separator tokens where scraped boilerplate or technical metadata gives way to descriptive prose — e.g. the newline after an HTML class-attribute string, an en-dash "–" after a CLI/product label, or boilerplate nouns like "release", "price", "key", "find"; it is suppressed on conversational first-person/second-person prose ("I", "you").
